newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - ASDA profits, performance on a roll.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - ASDA profits, performance on a roll.

text.p: British supermarket chain ASDA Plc turned in strong sales and an increase in year profits on Thursday as its chief executive said he expected the group to continue outpacing the rest of the industry.
"Do I believe that we can continue to outperform the industry? Yes, I do," Chief Executive Allan Leighton told Reuters in a telephone interview.

ASDA saw sales from existing stores up 9.2 percent in the year ending May 3 with pretax profits before exceptionals rising 16 percent to 353.7 million pounds ($588.1 million) as expected and paid out a total dividend of 3.05 pence per share, up from 2.65 pence.
Shares were up three pence to 125 pence by 1010 GMT, off a high of 126.5 pence.
"The numbers are good, showing a strong performance from a number of divisions, particularly clothing...I'd expect to see some upgrades today," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
ASDA should create up to 4,000 jobs during the year as it refurbishes five stores and opens another five, with a new distribution centre likely to push up total new jobs to 5,000, Leighton said.

He said he was "sure we will be able to help" the new Labour government in its plans for a new deal to combat youth unemployment, which involves offering subsidies to employers who take on young jobless.

ASDA is known for its cheeky and innovative image and its reputation as a champion of consumers by breaking price monopolies. It said market share increased to 11 percent from 10.1 percent a year ago as it focused on value for money over diversification into financial services like several of its competitors.
ASDA is the only one of Britain's big four supermarkets which does not offer a nationwide loyalty card and has not branched out into bank accounts or financial services.

Leighton said achieving such strong sales growth, one of the best in the industry, "becomes more and more difficult," but added that he expected the company to outperform "not just on sales but on operating profit too."
Leighton took over as chief executive last year from Archie Norman, the entrepreneur credited with turning the group round from heavy losses.
Norman stepped up to be chairman and has since become a member of parliament for the opposition Conservative party.
Leighton said ASDA's operating margins were roughly flat last year along with gross margins as it reinvested revenues from higher margin products back into lower prices.
The company said in a statement that industry figures showed it was eight percent cheaper than its major competitors, which include market leader Tesco, J. Sainsbury and Safeway.
Leighton said it was a key measure that the gap "is maintained or increased versus our competitors."
ASDA focuses on large, out-of-town superstores where it can offer non-food items such as clothing at discounts to the high street, providing it with a unique selling opportunity.

Leighton said he felt the clothing business, sold under the "George" brand set up with George Davis who worked with Next, could be twice the current size, which has seen sales rise 28 percent at existing stores.
"There's still a lot to do...to deliver this kind of performance consistently but I think we will," he said.
He said volume sales of clothing in the group's best stores were on similar levels to shops in the high street but operating costs were half.
"If I can sort the supply chain out...you can then generate a quality offer...at 20 percent of the price. That is a set of economics that nobody else can emulate," he said.
"The only way in a very mature marketplace that you can outperform and generate real return is you've got to innovate faster than anybody else," Leighton said.
($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
